items.title: Section: Kneeling in Humble Request, Preparing a Mind Ready to Receive a Boundless Treasury

items.zh: 有智有力勝菩薩所，謙下恭敬膝輪據地，或蹲、跪、坐，對佛像前，作如是請：唯願大德，或言長老、或善男子，哀愍授我菩薩淨戒。
items.en: Before the genuinely qualified bodhisattva, humbly and reverently, knees to the ground — whether squatting, kneeling, or sitting — facing an image of the Buddha, one voices this request: I ask only, venerable one — or elder, or good sir — that out of compassion you grant me the pure precepts of a bodhisattva.

items.zh: 如是請已，專念一境長養淨心，我今不久當得無盡、無量、無上大功德藏，即隨思惟如是事義，默然而住。
items.en: Having made this request, one focuses the mind single-pointedly, cultivating a genuinely pure heart: I shall soon attain an inexhaustible, boundless, unsurpassed treasury of merit — reflecting on this very meaning, one settles into quiet, focused stillness.

items.title: Section: The Formal Questions — Are You a Bodhisattva? Have You Made the Vow? Will You Receive?

items.zh: 爾時有智有力菩薩，於彼能行正行菩薩，以無亂心，若坐、若立而作是言：汝如是名善男子聽、或法弟聽，汝是菩薩不？彼應答言：是！發菩提願未？應答言：已發！
items.en: The qualified bodhisattva then says: listen, good sir so-and-so, or, dharma brother — are you a bodhisattva? The candidate answers: I am! Have you given rise to the aspiration towards awakening? The candidate answers: I have!

items.zh: 汝如是名善男子、或法弟，欲於我所受諸菩薩一切學處，受諸菩薩一切淨戒。謂律儀戒、攝善法戒、饒益有情戒。如是學處、如是淨戒，過去一切菩薩已具，未來一切菩薩當具，普於十方現在一切菩薩今具。於是學處、於是淨戒，過去一切菩薩已學，未來一切菩薩當學，現在一切菩薩今學。汝能受不？答言：能受！能授菩薩第二、第三亦如是說，能受菩薩第二、第三亦如是答。
items.en: Good sir so-and-so, or dharma brother, do you wish to receive from me every bodhisattva discipline, every pure bodhisattva precept — restraint discipline, discipline gathering wholesome practice, and discipline benefiting beings? These very disciplines and precepts, every bodhisattva of the past has already held them, every bodhisattva of the present across the ten directions holds them now, and every bodhisattva of the future will hold them. ... Are you able to receive them? The candidate answers: I am able! This exchange is repeated a second and third time in exactly the same words.

items.zh: 能授菩薩作如是問，乃至第三授淨戒已。能受菩薩作如是答，乃至第三受淨戒已。能受菩薩不起于坐。能授菩薩對佛像前，普於十方現住諸佛及諸菩薩恭敬供養，

items.title: Section: Requesting the Buddhas and Advanced Bodhisattvas as Witnesses

items.zh: 頂禮雙足，作如是白：某名菩薩，今已於我某菩薩所，乃至三說受菩薩戒，我某菩薩已為某名菩薩作證。
items.en: Bowing at the Buddha's feet, one reports: the bodhisattva so-and-so has now, before me, spoken three times to receive the bodhisattva precepts; I, the bodhisattva so-and-so, have already served as witness to that.

items.zh: 唯願十方無邊無際諸世界中諸佛菩薩第一真聖，於現不現一切時處一切有情皆現覺者，於此某名受戒菩薩亦為作證。第二、第三，亦如是說。
items.en: I ask only that the buddhas, foremost of all beings, and the truly noble bodhisattvas who have entered the great grounds, across the boundless worlds of the ten directions, whose awareness reaches every being at every time and place, whether present or not, likewise serve as witnesses for this bodhisattva so-and-so, now receiving the precepts. This too is spoken a second and third time.

items.title: Section: How the Ordination Registers Across Reality — Like an Image in a Polished Mirror

items.zh: 如是受戒羯磨畢竟。從此無間，普於十方無邊無際諸世界中現住諸佛、已入大地諸菩薩前，法爾相現。由此表示如是菩薩已受菩薩所受淨戒。
items.en: Once this ordination ceremony is genuinely complete, immediately and without any gap, this very image naturally arises before the presently living buddhas and bodhisattvas already established on the noble grounds, across the boundless worlds of the ten directions — this is precisely how it is shown that this bodhisattva has now received the bodhisattva precepts.

items.zh: 爾時十方諸佛菩薩，於是菩薩法爾之相生起憶念；由憶念故，正智見轉；由正智見，如實覺知：某世界中某名菩薩，某菩薩所正受菩薩所受淨戒。
items.en: At that very moment, buddhas and bodhisattvas across the ten directions naturally give rise to awareness of this bodhisattva's own image; through that awareness, genuine, realised knowledge arises; and through that genuine knowledge, they truly know: in such-and-such a world, the bodhisattva so-and-so has, before the bodhisattva so-and-so, genuinely received the bodhisattva precepts.

items.title: Section: Parental Love From Every Buddha, and the Ceremony Concludes

items.zh: 一切於此受戒菩薩，如子如弟，生親善意，眷念憐愍。由佛菩薩眷念憐愍，令是菩薩希求善法倍復增長，無有退減。
items.en: All buddhas and bodhisattvas regard this newly ordained bodhisattva as their own child or younger sibling, giving rise to genuine warmth and care. Through this care, the new bodhisattva's own wish to pursue wholesome practice grows all the more, never quietly declining.

items.zh: 當知是名受菩薩戒啟白請證。
如是已作受菩薩戒羯磨等事，授受菩薩俱起供養，普於十方無邊無際諸世界中諸佛菩薩，頂禮雙足恭敬而退。
items.en: The ordination ceremony now genuinely complete, the preceptor and the newly ordained bodhisattva rise together to make offerings, bow at the feet of the buddhas and bodhisattvas across the boundless worlds of the ten directions, and respectfully withdraw.

items.title: Section: The Supreme Benefits of the Bodhisattva Precepts — Beyond All Comparison

items.zh: 如是菩薩所受律儀戒，於餘一切所受律儀戒最勝無上，無量無邊大功德藏之所隨逐，第一最上善心意樂之所發起，普能對治於一切有情一切種惡行。
items.en: A bodhisattva's own restraint discipline is, among all other forms of restraint received by anyone, the most excellent and unsurpassed — accompanied by a boundless treasury of merit, arising from the single greatest and most excellent wholesome aspiration, and able to universally counter every kind of wrongdoing in every being.

items.zh: 一切別解脫律儀，於此菩薩律儀戒百分不及一，千分不及一，數分不及一，計分不及一，算分不及一，喻分不及一，鄔波尼殺曇分亦不及一，攝受一切大功德故。
items.en: Every individually liberating precept, compared to this bodhisattva restraint discipline, does not come within one part in a hundred, one part in a thousand, nor any countable, calculable, or even metaphorically expressible fraction, not even the most infinitesimal conceivable portion — since this discipline gathers in the whole of every great merit there is.

items.title: Section: A Practical Framework for What a Bodhisattva Should and Should Not Do

items.zh: 又此菩薩安住如是菩薩淨戒，先自數數專諦思惟：此是菩薩正所應作，此非菩薩正所應作。既思惟已，然後為成正所作業，當勤修學。
items.en: A bodhisattva abiding in these pure precepts first repeatedly and earnestly reflects: this is genuinely what a bodhisattva should do, this is not what a bodhisattva should do. Having reflected in this way, they then diligently train so as to actually accomplish what is genuinely right.

items.title: Diligently Studying the Scriptures and Their Commentaries — Why a Commentary Is Called a "Mother"

items.zh: 又應專勵聽聞菩薩素怛纜藏及以解釋，即此菩薩素怛纜藏、摩怛履迦，隨其所聞當勤修學。
items.en: One should also diligently seek out and study the Great Vehicle's own scriptures together with their commentaries — these very scriptures and their commentaries — diligently training in whatever one has the opportunity to hear.

blocks.text: The ceremony itself, word by word. It is still performed in this form today.
Kneeling before the preceptor, "facing an image of the Buddha", the candidate asks. Then "focusing the mind single-pointedly: I shall soon attain an inexhaustible, unsurpassed treasury of merit".

"Listen, good friend so-and-so, dharma brother: are you a bodhisattva?" "I am!" "Have you given rise to the aspiration towards awakening?" "I have!" "Do you wish to receive from me every bodhisattva training and pure precept: restraint, gathering the good, benefiting beings, the precepts all past, future, and present bodhisattvas have trained in?" "I do." Asked three times. Master Cháng Bǎi: say it clearly; if too soft, the ceremony is not complete.

The preceptor bows before the Buddha: "The bodhisattva so-and-so has, before me, three times asked to receive the bodhisattva precepts. I ask the Buddhas and the noble bodhisattvas of the ten directions, whose awareness reaches everywhere, to bear witness."

subs.head: Like an image in a mirror

blocks.text: "Immediately and without gap, this image naturally appears before the Buddhas and bodhisattvas" of every direction. Master Cháng Bǎi: like a polished, spotless mirror. "All Buddhas and bodhisattvas regard this newly ordained bodhisattva as their own child or younger sibling."
"Among all forms of restraint, the bodhisattva's is most excellent"; "every prātimokṣa precept compared to it does not come within one part in a hundred".

The bodhisattva reflects: "this is what a bodhisattva should do; this is not", and studies the bodhisattva canon with its commentaries (Venerable Miào Jìng: a commentary is the "mother" from which wisdom grows).

quiz.q: The English reads only "humbly and reverently kneeling, facing an image of the Buddha." What is missing?
options: the treatise gives three postures — squatting, kneeling, or sitting — but the English keeps only kneeling
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: generally one kneels upright facing the Buddha image. Venerable Miào Jìng: the knee is round, so it is called a "wheel." The English drops squatting and sitting.

quiz.q: What are the first two questions the preceptor formally asks the candidate?
options: Are you a bodhisattva? Have you made the vow towards awakening?
How old are you? Do you have money?
Are you ordained? Do you chant?
Do you believe? Are you vegetarian?
quiz.why: "Are you a bodhisattva? The candidate answers: I am! Have you given rise to the aspiration towards awakening? The candidate answers: I have!" Master Cháng Bǎi: this confirms the candidate has the bodhisattva lineage.

quiz.q: When the candidate answers "I can receive!", what does Master Cháng Bǎi remind us?
options: say it loudly — if too soft, the preceptor will say the ceremony is invalid
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one must also say it loudly — if it's too soft, the preceptor will say the ceremony did not take effect.

quiz.q: The English merges this into "the genuinely realised buddhas and bodhisattvas." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish "foremost" and "truly noble"?
options: "foremost" refers to the buddhas; "truly noble" to bodhisattvas already established on the grounds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "foremost" here refers to the buddhas; "truly noble" means bodhisattvas, restricted to those already on the grounds. The English merges the two.

quiz.q: When the ceremony is complete, an image "naturally appears" before the buddhas. What simile do the lectures use?
options: like a well-polished, spotless mirror; Miào Jìng: "yíng" means to polish
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: like the surface of a well-polished, clean mirror, wiped spotless. Venerable Miào Jìng: "yíng" means polishing or wiping.

quiz.q: "Not even one upaniṣad-part." The English reads "not even the most infinitesimal conceivable portion." How do the lectures explain upaniṣad?
options: in Chinese it means "cause"; Cháng Bǎi: the comparison is in terms of cause and effect
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: upaniṣad is rendered in Chinese as "cause." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the cause, a comparison in terms of cause and effect. The English takes only the sense of "infinitesimal."

quiz.q: Abiding in the pure precepts, what does the bodhisattva first repeatedly reflect on?
options: when one may give them up
this is what a bodhisattva should do; this is not
quiz.why: "First repeatedly and earnestly reflects: this is genuinely what a bodhisattva should do, this is not." Master Cháng Bǎi: a bodhisattva who has received the precepts must have the wisdom to know what should and should not be done.
